title: Pulled-Back Symplectic Facet Setup
body_html:
Pulled-Back Symplectic Facet Setup

Let $F_0$ be a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic. Fix a non-trivial additive character

$$ \psi:F_0\to\mathbb{C}^\times . $$

Let $D$ be the division algebra with involution used for the dual pair, and let $\mathfrak{o}_D$ be its maximal order.

Let

$$ (G,G')=(U(V,h),U(V',h')) $$

be a reductive dual pair, where $V$ and $V'$ are right $D$-modules, $h$ is $\varepsilon$-Hermitian, and $h'$ is $(-\varepsilon)$-Hermitian. Let

$$ W=V\otimes_D V' $$

be the associated symplectic $F$-space.

For

$$ z=(x,x')\in B(G)\times B(G'), $$

let $\mathcal{L}_x$ and $\mathcal{L}'_{x'}$ be the corresponding self-dual lattice functions on $V$ and $V'$. Define the tensor lattice function on $W$ by

$$ \mathcal{B}_{z,t} := \mathcal{B}_{x,x',t} := (\mathcal{L}_x\otimes_D\mathcal{L}'_{x'})_t = \sum_{t=t_1+t_2} \mathcal{L}_{x,t_1}\otimes_{\mathfrak{o}_D}\mathcal{L}'_{x',t_2}. $$

Equivalently, using $W\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_D(V,V')$,

$$ \mathcal{B}_{x,x',t} = \bigcap_r \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak{o}_D} (\mathcal{L}_{x,r},\mathcal{L}'_{x',t+r}). $$

This gives an affine embedding

$$ \iota: B(G)\times B(G') \longrightarrow B(\operatorname{Sp}(W)), \qquad z=(x,x')\longmapsto \mathcal{B}_z. $$

In applications one may replace $B(G)\times B(G')$ by a sub-building product such as $B(G^0)\times B(G'^0)$. For the transition-map problem, write

$$ X:=B(G)\times B(G') $$

unless a smaller domain is explicitly imposed.

The relevant facet structure on $X$ is the pullback of the symplectic-building facet structure along $\iota$, not the naive product facet structure.

Define $\mathcal{P}$ to be the set of non-empty connected polyhedral components of

$$ \iota^{-1}(\mathfrak{f}), \qquad \mathfrak{f}\in\operatorname{Fac}(\operatorname{Sp}(W)). $$

For $F\in\mathcal{P}$, let

$$ \mathfrak{f}_F\subset B(\operatorname{Sp}(W)) $$

be the unique symplectic facet such that

$$ F\subseteq \iota^{-1}(\mathfrak{f}_F). $$

Define incidence in $\mathcal{P}$ by

$$ E\leq F \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad E\subseteq \overline F $$

inside $X$. In the transition-map problem, this incidence convention is taken to imply

$$ \mathfrak{f}_E\subseteq \overline{\mathfrak{f}_F} $$

inside $B(\operatorname{Sp}(W))$.

For $F\in\mathcal{P}$, choose any $z\in F$. Since $\iota(F)$ lies in one symplectic facet, the lattices

$$ L_F:=\mathcal{B}_{z,0}, \qquad L_F^+:=\mathcal{B}_{z,0^+} $$

are treated as independent of $z\in F$. This pulled-back facet structure is part of the fixed input for the transition-map problem, not a target to be re-proved.
